title: Bonnie Rotten
summary: A two-hour ensemble episode that moves from faith, prison and recovery into Bonnie Rotten's professional history, workplace boundaries, explicit performance accounts, health folklore, condom-policy debate, a continually changing proposed sex-tape production, Money Mark's creative work and trivia. Every idea is preserved. The editorial layer distinguishes testimony from fact, fantasy from completed conduct, narrow permission from blanket consent, and private people from public professional identities.
source_notes: The immutable audio and raw/clean transcript artifacts are present in the shared local corpus.
All four cleaner removals are empty zero-duration records; no spoken line was removed by those edits.
The automated anomaly pass found no segment above compression 2.4, below average log probability -0.9, or above no-speech probability 0.7.
The low-confidence Bonnie Rodden suggestion is accepted as Bonnie Rotten because the episode title, repeated introduction and guest context all resolve the public professional name.
Global David Chosex replacement is accepted only where it is clearly the David Choe sex-tape wordplay; it is not a general vocabulary token.

NIDDK says adult rectal prolapse can worsen, damage sphincter muscles and nerves, and become an emergency if it cannot be pushed back; absence of pain is not a safety finding: https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/digestive-diseases/anatomic-problems-lower-gi-tract/rectal-prolapse

CDC says bacterial vaginosis is a vaginal bacterial imbalance associated with sexual activity, lack of condom use, new or multiple partners and douching; it is not exclusively caused by sitting on a bench without underwear: https://www.cdc.gov/bacterial-vaginosis/about/index.html
The clean layer has zero diarized turns and zero voice windows, so the transcript remains dialogue-unnamed despite several explicit in-room introductions.

Thirty-six narrow spans protect private peers, relatives, disputed debts, messages, intimate footage, medical details, schedules, contact paths and nonparticipating prospective performers. They do not delete or soften the ideas.
speaker_policy: Participant names may be stated in editorial context when explicitly introduced or publicly credited, but no transcript line is assigned to a named speaker. Zero turns and zero identity windows cannot support independently validated named dialogue.

connections.why: The speaker describes born-again Christianity as genuine survival scaffolding, then explains why his theology changed.
Higher-power framing is discussed as useful without requiring one religion.
Charity and time-giving are presented as repayment of a prison promise.
Bonnie Rotten is explicitly introduced by her public work name; private peers remain distinct.
Anger management is voluntary and framed as controlling one's response, not other people.
The Taco Bell fight and debt dispute are testimony, not adjudicated fact.
Tattoo coverage is described as a predicted career barrier that the guest overcame.
Eyes-closed portraits are simultaneously an aesthetic choice, time-saver and source of projected depth.
A public work can be indexed without treating performers or masked extras as generally accessible.
A person physically present at a shoot may still be unauthorized and removable.
Professional agreement does not erase specific-act boundaries or preferences about a spouse's presence.
Painless rectal prolapse is not harmless and may worsen or require treatment.
The show repeatedly calls itself therapy while recognizing that it rewards escalation.
Vaginal looseness, condom stretching and profession-based anatomy claims are unreliable.
The guest says she followed pushing instructions without understanding prolapse and objected afterward.
Owning intimate footage does not require releasing it, even under an anti-censorship identity.
An explicit enema description is preserved without becoming medical or procedural advice.
The condom debate combines labor autonomy, business impact, testing claims and resistance to state oversight.
The bench/no-panties account is not a reliable exclusive cause of bacterial infection.
The orgy proposal directly continues the previous episode's unstable consent discussion.
Participants repeatedly enter, qualify, withdraw and re-enter rather than giving one permanent answer.
Fan demand for proof cannot authorize filming or publication for participants.
Permission for one breast to be touched is a literal example of act- and body-part-specific consent.
Participants say they cannot decide because motel fun, professional production and commercial tape keep replacing one another.
The group explicitly corrects the demand that a participant must orgasm for the production.
A sleep fantasy can be staged with advance consent; an actually sleeping person cannot consent in the moment.
The guest describes converting performance success into ownership and production.
Money Mark connects the episode to Damon Albarn, William Onyeabor, film scoring and collaborative music.
Sexual repetition, masturbation and nonstop music-making are compared as obsession rather than simple passion.
The episode argues that refusing to release every explicit image is artistic selection, not denial that it exists.
